obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Cloud Software
applies: Yes (primary rule for the focus division)
basis: A for-profit business in commerce, not in a 45(a)(2) carve-out, with no size threshold. The division makes security and data-use statements in its trust center, product pages, DPAs and SOC 2 description, and holds data on about 21 million workers

obligation: FTC Act Section 5: Technology Consulting, Payments and Payroll, group
applies: Yes (statements and practices; not the primary analysis)
basis: Each is a for-profit business in commerce. Consulting makes client-facing statements and uses a delivery AI tool; the FTC also enforces Part 314 for Payments and Payroll; group statements include the trust center and the Item 106 text

obligation: COPPA Rule: all divisions and group
basis: Workforce Cloud is a business service sold to employers for their workforces, not directed to children under 13; no division operates a child-directed service

obligation: CCPA and CPPA regulations, cybersecurity audit: group
citation: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.140(d); Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, 7120-7124
basis: The group is a CCPA business (revenue test met) and in 2025 processed personal information of more than 250,000 California consumers as a business, which meets 7120(b)(2)(A); with 2026 revenue over $100 million the first report is due 2028-04-01

obligation: CCPA service-provider duties: Cloud Software
citation: Cal. Civ. Code 1798.140 (service provider and business definitions)
applies: Yes (service provider for customer data; business for its own data)
basis: Customers are businesses whose worker data the WCP processes under DPAs with CCPA service-provider terms; about 2.3 million worker profiles are California residents

obligation: CCPA ADMT and risk assessment rules: group HR and Cloud Software customers
citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11, 7200 et seq. (ADMT); risk assessment articles
basis: Group HR, a CCPA business, uses an automated tool to rank applicants for hiring, including California applicants. Cloud Software customers that are CCPA businesses may use attrition-risk scores for significant decisions, so the division as service provider must give them what they need

obligation: CCPA: Payments and Payroll customer information
applies: Partly (GLBA data exempt at the data level, except the 1798.150 breach private right of action)
basis: Payroll and payment customer information is subject to GLBA through the FTC Safeguards Rule

obligation: DOJ Data Security Program: all divisions and group
basis: The WCP and the payroll engine hold covered personal identifiers on more than 100,000 people and personal financial data on more than 10,000 (bulk thresholds, 28 CFR 202.205). No offshore hosting and no staff or vendors in a country of concern are recorded; vendor screening does not ask about ownership by covered persons

obligation: PADFA: all divisions and group
basis: PADFA reaches data brokers. The group processes customer and worker data to provide its services and does not sell or license it to third parties

obligation: FCC CPNI rules: all divisions and group
basis: No division is a telecommunications carrier or interconnected VoIP provider

obligation: FedRAMP: Cloud Software
basis: Workforce Cloud has no government edition; the consulting division's federal clients use other cloud products

obligation: SEC cybersecurity disclosure (also N52-R08): group
basis: The holding company is an SEC registrant; divisions contribute incident facts through the group and the disclosure committee

obligation: GLBA privacy and safeguards: Payments and Payroll
applies: Yes (safeguards, through the FTC Safeguards Rule, N52-R03)
basis: Group legal treats the division as a financial institution because it regularly transfers money for workers and merchants. The safeguards duty is analyzed through 16 CFR Part 314; GLBA privacy notice duties are not analyzed in this sample

obligation: Interagency Guidelines Establishing Information Security Standards: all divisions
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B; 12 CFR 208 App. D-2 and 225 App. F; 12 CFR 364 App. B
basis: No subsidiary holds a bank charter. Cloud Software's duty toward its bank and credit union customers is the bank service provider notice (row BSP-NOTICE)

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: Payments and Payroll
basis: Group legal decided in 2024 to treat the division as a financial institution under 314.2(h) and to apply Part 314 to all payroll and payment data it handles. The 314.6 exceptions do not apply: the division holds customer information on about 2.4 million workers and tens of thousands of merchant principals

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule, service provider oversight: Cloud Software as affiliate custodian
applies: Yes (through Payments and Payroll's oversight duty)
basis: The WCP stores the division's customer information (the payroll handoff files) as a service to it, which makes the WCP a service provider the division must select, contract with and assess
analyzed_in: P03 (gap-analysis-payments-and-payroll.csv PY-G19 to PY-G21; gap-analysis.csv); P02

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule: Technology Consulting
basis: The division provides implementation, integration and managed application services; it does not prepare tax returns or perform other financial activities

obligation: NYDFS Cybersecurity Regulation: all divisions
basis: No subsidiary holds a New York license

obligation: SEC Regulation S-P: all divisions
basis: Reg S-P applies to brokers, dealers, investment companies, registered investment advisers and transfer agents. The subsidiaries' businesses are SaaS, consulting, and payroll and payment services; none is described as any of these

obligation: SEC Regulation S-ID: all divisions
basis: Reg S-ID applies to SEC-regulated financial entities such as broker-dealers and investment advisers; no subsidiary is one

obligation: NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law #668: all divisions
citation: NAIC Model #668 as enacted by each state
basis: No subsidiary holds an insurance license

obligation: NCUA security program and incident notification: all divisions
basis: Part 748 binds federally insured credit unions; no subsidiary is a credit union. Cloud Software's duty toward its credit union customers is the bank service provider notice (row BSP-NOTICE)

obligation: OCC heightened standards: all divisions
basis: No subsidiary holds a bank charter

obligation: IRC 7216 preparer disclosure limits: Technology Consulting
basis: The division prepares no tax returns; its services are implementation, integration and managed application services

obligation: IRS Publication 4557 WISP expectation: Technology Consulting
basis: The publication addresses tax professionals; the division is not one

obligation: FAR basic safeguarding: Technology Consulting
citation: 48 CFR 52.204-21 (52.240-93 in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation)
basis: The clause appears in the 14 federal civilian agency contracts, and consultants' systems hold federal contract information. Workforce Cloud and the Payments and Payroll services hold no federal contracts with the clause

obligation: FAR covered telecommunications reporting: Technology Consulting
citation: 48 CFR 52.204-25 and 52.204-23 (52.240-91 under a class deviation)
basis: The same contracts contain the clauses; the federal practice buys some hardware for agency projects

obligation: DFARS 252.204-7012 and CMMC: all divisions
basis: No DoD contracts; none of the 14 federal contracts designates CUI or contains DFARS clauses

obligation: HIPAA business associate duties: Technology Consulting
basis: BAAs are signed with all 31 hospital and health-system clients; nurse-staffing integrations take EHR census feeds, and for 9 clients patient-level ADT data passes through test environments

obligation: HIPAA: Cloud Software, Payments and Payroll, group
basis: No PHI is held in the WCP (only staffing counts pass into tenants from consulting's integrations), and the payroll and payment services are not health plans, providers or clearinghouses or business associates of one

obligation: ABA Model Rules as adopted in Florida: Technology Consulting
basis: The rules bind lawyers; the division provides IT services, not legal services

obligation: AICPA Code of Professional Conduct: Technology Consulting
basis: A professional standard for CPA firms and members; the division is not a CPA firm

obligation: CIRCIA: all divisions and group
basis: No final rule as of the sample date; the group would likely be in scope as an entity above the SBA size standard in a critical infrastructure sector if the final rule keeps the proposed criterion. Tracked

obligation: Bank service provider notification: Cloud Software
applies: Yes (about 420 bank and credit union customers)
basis: Counsel treats the division as a bank service provider to its bank and credit union customers; notice is owed to a bank-designated contact when an incident disrupts covered services for 4 or more hours

obligation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 (contract): Payments and Payroll
citation: PCI DSS v4.0.1; sponsor bank B agreement and card network rules
basis: The payments platform accepts cards for about 26,000 merchants and validates with an annual Report on Compliance. WCP pages that embed checkout are in the division's scope reviews; the WCP holds no account data

obligation: Money transmission (federal and state): Payments and Payroll
applies: Open question (counsel review; no conclusion asserted)
basis: The payroll funds flow moves employer money to workers through sponsor bank A's accounts; outside counsel's state-by-state review started in 2025 and is not complete

obligation: Florida Information Protection Act and other state breach laws: all divisions
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171; each state where affected individuals reside
basis: The WCP holds personal information on about 1.6 million Florida workers and the payroll engine on about 190,000; employees work in 44 states and customers' workers live in all 50. Florida is the worked example

obligation: Colorado SB26-189 (AI in consequential decisions): Cloud Software and group HR
applies: Yes (from 2027-01-01): Cloud Software as developer of attrition-risk insights; group HR as deployer of resume screening. Merchant risk scoring under counsel review
basis: Attrition-risk scores reach customers' employment decisions; group HR ranks applicants with an automated tool

obligation: Title VII, ADEA and UGESP adverse impact guidance: group HR
basis: The group is an employer of 45,000 people and screens applicants with an automated ranking tool

obligation: OFAC ransomware payment advisory: group
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021)
basis: Sanctions screening applies to any ransom payment decision by a U.S. person

obligation: HIPAA Security Rule NPRM: Technology Consulting
basis: Not a final rule; tracked for the consulting business associate work

obligation: FTC proposed AI-accuracy policy statement: Cloud Software
basis: Not final; tracked against the AI product claims

obligation: Workforce Cloud customer DPAs and MSA: Cloud Software
basis: Incident notice within 72 hours of confirmation (48 hours for about 1,240 customers); 30 days' sub-processor notice; deletion within 90 days; customer data used only to provide the service; 99.95% monthly availability

obligation: SOC 2 and SOC 1 commitments: Cloud Software and Payments and Payroll
citation: AICPA Trust Services Criteria; SSAE 18; customer contracts
applies: Yes (contract): Workforce Cloud SOC 2 Type 2 yearly; SOC 1 Type 2 for payroll; first Payments and Payroll SOC 2 planned; Technology Consulting out of scope
basis: The MSA promises a current SOC 2 report; employers rely on the SOC 1 report

obligation: Sponsor bank program agreements: Payments and Payroll
citation: Sponsor bank A and B program agreements
basis: Notice to each bank within 24 hours of determining a security incident that affects program data or disrupts program services

obligation: Client contracts and hospital BAAs: Technology Consulting
basis: Client data retention terms, client opt-in for generative AI use, and hospital BAA notice terms (5 to 30 days)

obligation: Intercompany services agreements: group
basis: The 2024 agreement covers the checkout embedded in WCP pages; no agreement covers the payroll handoff
